decisions.reason: The address autocomplete service was publicly announced as a new web service and sits on shared address data infrastructure, so sunk investment, the visible commitment and low running costs favour keeping it.

The Austrian gas grid fee database extends the firm's announced energy-data direction into a new market, and weak uptake can still be blamed on the temporary difficulty of entering that market, so management persists.
Peak load window determination is a niche regulatory service tied to the firm's core grid-fee expertise, and its centrality to the announced energy focus justifies continued commitment.

The end-customer tariff database is central to the firm's energy data offering and likely shares data pipelines with existing products, so dropping it would undercut earlier investment and positioning.
Custom web services are a flexible offering built on the firm's existing consulting and programming capabilities, cost little to maintain and fit its identity.
The postal code lookup service is a low-cost companion to the address products that rests on infrastructure the firm has already paid for, so there is little reason to abandon it.
